 3 weather alerts in effect Federal officials warn Nevadans of surge in holiday shopping fraud 
 U.S. Marshals Service says scammers are getting more aggressive this time of year 
 Federal officials say scammers may use fake invoices and urgent payment demands during the holiday season. By Miles Friess Published : Nov. 18, 2026 at 8:15 PM PST | Updated : 8 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google LAS VEGAS ( FOX5 ) — Holiday shopping season is here, and federal officials are warning people in Nevada to watch for a surge in fraud.
 The U.S. Marshals Service in Nevada said scammers are getting more aggressive this time of year. AARP said four out of five U.S. adults have been targeted by at least one common fraud or holiday scam.
 Common scam tactics
 One red flag is anyone demanding payment with gift cards or cryptocurrency. Scammers will pretend there is an emergency, an unpaid fine or a fake arrest warrant and try to rush people into paying.
 Another common trick involves emails or texts with fake invoices. The messages claim a large charge on a PayPal account or credit card and tell the recipient to click a link to confirm or cancel.
 MORE ON FOX5: Nevada National Guard to support police at Formula One race in Las Vegas 
 What experts recommend
 Experts say people should hang up on unexpected calls, not give out personal or financial information, and not click links from unknown or suspicious senders.
 Anyone worried about a charge should open a new browser window, go straight to their bank, credit card or PayPal website, sign in and check their recent transactions themselves.
 Federal officials said people should not take the bait and should protect their money and identity.
 For more tips on protecting yourself and your family against holiday fraud, read AARP’s guide .
